claim: Local preference is the BGP attribute AWS recommends for active/passive connections when the advertised prefix lengths are the same.
question: Which BGP attribute does AWS recommend for active/passive Direct Connect paths with equal prefix lengths?

values.display: Local preference is the BGP attribute recommended to use when desired routing paths are meant for active/passive connections
the prefix lengths advertised are the same

evidence.quote: Local preference is the BGP attribute recommended to use when desired routing paths are meant for active/passive connections and the prefix lengths advertised are the same.

claim: Direct Connect can lower network cost in two ways: you reduce the bandwidth costs paid to your internet service provider, and data transferred over your dedicated connection is charged at the reduced Direct Connect data transfer rate instead of internet rates.
question: How can Direct Connect reduce network cost compared with the internet?

values.display: you can reduce your bandwidth costs paid to your internet service provider
charged at the reduced AWS Direct Connect data transfer rate, rather than internet data transfer rates

qualifiers.scope: Direct Connect compared with internet data transfer

evidence.quote: First, by transferring data to and from AWS directly, you can reduce your bandwidth costs paid to your internet service provider. Second, all data transferred over your dedicated connection is charged at the reduced AWS Direct Connect data transfer rate, rather than internet data transfer rates – see the Direct Connect pricing page for details.
